description: The presentation: its theme, slides, and settings.

markdownpoint.description: The format version, as a major and a minor number in quotes: "1.0".

id.description: The presentation's id. The .md file has the same id.

save-id.description: A save stamp, the id of a save. MarkdownPoint writes it while the presentation is shared for editing. Other tools leave it unchanged.

theme.description: The key of the presentation's theme. It's the name of the theme's folder in themes. The theme's master sets the slide size and `unit-scale`.

background.description: The background every slide shows, unless the slide sets its own.

transition.description: The transition from every slide to the next, unless the slide sets its own. Without it, slides cross-dissolve over 0.5 seconds.

soundtrack.description: Music that plays under the whole presentation.

file.description: The audio file, as a presentation's file path.

loop.description: `repeat` plays it again from the start when it ends. Without a loop, it plays once.

fade-in.description: How long it takes to rise linearly from silence each time it starts.

fade-out.description: How long it takes to fall linearly to silence before the file ends each time. Where the two fades overlap, the lower volume is used.

self-playing.description: Settings for playing the presentation by itself, such as at a kiosk.

slide-delay.description: How long each slide stays after its last step before the next slide.

step-delay.description: How long the presentation waits before each step that would wait for a click.

loop.description: `repeat` starts it over after the last slide. Without a loop, it stops there.

countdown.description: How long the talk should take, in seconds. The presenter's timer counts down from it.

anyOf.description: What a new text box starts with. Without this key, or with an empty record, a new text box uses the body style. `"none"` gives it no style.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

default-text-style.description: The text style and color of a new text box, or none for no style.

image-style.description: The style generated image objects use when they don't set one. It's written as text, and `none`, the default, means no style. A background's picture uses `background-image-style` instead.

background-image-style.description: The style generated background images use when their background doesn't set one. It's written as text, and `none`, the default, means no style.

swatches.description: The colors the author has saved for this presentation, as hex colors.

date.description: The date the date field shows, as YYYY-MM-DD. It must be a real calendar date, from year 0001 on.

locale.description: The presentation's language and region, as a BCP 47 tag such as fr-CA. It sets how the date field is written, chart cells are read, and words are split to animate. The default is en-US.

additionalProperties.description: One slide's objects, look, and animation. Its text is in the .md file.

layout.description: The theme layout the slide uses, by key.

scheme.description: The slide's color scheme. If it's left out or the theme doesn't have it, the slide uses its layout's scheme.

background.description: The slide's own background. It replaces the presentation's whole background. A key it leaves out has its default, and an empty background is plain.

skipped.description: Whether the slide is skipped when presenting and exporting. It stays in the presentation.

transition.description: The transition from this slide to the next, or none.

The camera's motion blur. Only the 3D layer blurs, and only in exported movies and the Agent's rendered frames. The editor, presentations, and still exports stay sharp.

shutter.description: How long the shutter stays open, in frames of the movie. 0 draws no blur. Left out, it's 0.5. A step can animate it.

frame-position.description: Where the frame's moment falls in the shutter's opening. Left out, it's center.

samples.description: How many moments the 3D layer is drawn at while the shutter is open, then averaged, as Cinema 4D's Sub-Frame Motion Blur Samples. Left out, it's 32.

anyOf.description: The camera's render effects, as Cinema 4D's Render Settings add Global Illumination and Ambient Occlusion: a fast estimate of light bouncing between surfaces and of the World's light closed off where they meet. It shows wherever the 3D layer does. Only surfaces in view bounce light, and a shadow catcher bounces none. An override replaces the whole record.

global-illumination.description: Whether lit surfaces bounce their light onto what stands near them. Left out, it's false.

ambient-occlusion.description: Whether the World's light darkens where surfaces close in on each other, and a shadow catcher darkens where an object stands on it. Left out, it's false.

distance.description: How far bounced light and shading reach from a surface. Left out, it's 400.

anyOf.description: The camera's drift: on the slide's own clock, which starts as its transition in begins and runs on through its steps, waits and transition out, the camera and its target move together from `from` toward the camera's set position, standing `from` × (1 − t ÷ `duration`)² away from it t seconds after the start, so they slow steadily to rest. Stills and the editor show the set position, and a slide a scroll transition enters or leaves has no drift.

from.description: Where the camera starts, as an {x, y, z} offset from its set position. An axis left out doesn't move.

duration.description: How many seconds after the slide begins to appear the camera comes to rest.

anyOf.description: A constraint that moves the slide's camera with an object, as Cinema 4D's Position constraint does. Only the camera takes it. With a spring, the camera follows the way a keyframe's spring moves: it trails a sudden move, catches up, and settles as the object stops. A spring still moving 10 seconds after what it follows has stopped stands where it got to, short of its target, until a click moves what it follows again. Keys other than id, type, and target may be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as follow, unique among the camera's constraints. A step animates its strength as constraints.follow.strength.

target.description: The id of the model or light the camera follows.

target-node.description: The name of a node in the target's model, such as ball. The camera follows it where the model's Action moves it. Left out, the camera follows the target's origin.

axes.description: The 3D space's axes the camera follows on, of x, y, and z. Left out, all three.

relative-to-target.description: Whether the camera's position counts from the target's point instead of the slide's center at z 0, as Blender's Copy Location Offset adds it. Left out, it's true. False puts it at the target's point.

strength.description: How far the camera moves to the target's point, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. Left out, it's 1. A step can animate it.

spring.description: The spring the camera follows on, written as a keyframe's `spring` interpolation is: its `amount` and `response`. Left out, the camera follows exactly.

amount.description: How far the camera swings past where the target stops, from 0, not at all, to 1.

response.description: The spring's natural period. A shorter response catches up sooner.

overrides.description: Changes, by id, to what the slide inherits from its layout and master. They're kept even when they match what's inherited. `null` removes an object, except the camera and the World.

file.description: a file path in the presentation’s folder

objects.description: The slide's objects, back to front. Its own objects are written out, and one from its layout or master is listed by its id. An inherited object the list doesn't name is behind all of them.

initial.description: The values of animated parameters before the slide's first step, as "object.parameter" keys such as "card.opacity".

slides.description: The slides, by id. The .md file has their order and text.

additionalProperties.description: A reusable animated scene that slides show as instances. A composition can't contain itself, directly or through another.

name.description: The composition's name, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

scheme.description: The color scheme it's drawn in on its own canvas, where it's edited. The default is the light scheme. Each instance uses the scheme of the slide it's on.

items.description: One control a composition offers its instances, in the order they're shown. Its default matches its type: a number, true or false, a color, one of its options' ids, or a file path for a media control. The objects a media control binds are all of one media kind. Its default and values are of that kind too.

id.description: The id a binding, an instance's value, and a marker use for the control. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters. Two controls can have the same name.

id.description: The id a binding, an instance's value, and a marker use for the control. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

min.description: A number control's smallest value, below its max.

max.description: A number control's largest value, above its min.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

items.description: One option of a choice control, in the order its pop-up shows them.

id.description: The id the control's default, an instance's value, and a property the choice sets use for the option. It's unique among the control's options.

name.description: The words the author sees, on one line with no space at either end and no comma: ",", "，" or "、".

options.description: A choice control's options, one or more, in the order its pop-up shows them. Its default is one of their ids.

id.description: The id a binding, an instance's value, and a marker use for the control. It's unique among the composition's controls.

name.description: The name the author sees, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters. Two controls can have the same name.

default.description: The value used when an instance doesn't set one. A number control's default is from its min to its max. A text control's default text is in the .md file.

controls.description: What each instance can set, by control id.

objects.description: Its objects, back to front. A composition can't contain a model, a light, a shadow catcher, a floor, a camera, the World, or a text with a `model`.

initial.description: The values of animated parameters before its first step, as "object.parameter" keys.

steps.description: Its steps, played back to back. They have no cues and no `loop-from`. With every pass counted, they last at most 4,294,967,296 seconds.

compositions.description: Reusable animated scenes, by id. Slides show them as instances.

additionalProperties.description: A comment thread pinned to a slide or a composition, stored under an id unique among the presentation's threads.

slide.description: The id of the slide it is pinned to.

composition.description: The id of the composition it is pinned to.

created.description: When it was written, as a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z.

text.description: What it says, as text that isn't blank, without control characters but line breaks and tabs.

position.description: Where it is pinned, as {x, y} fractions of the slide or composition.

resolved.description: Whether the thread is resolved. Left out, it isn't.

additionalProperties.description: One reply in a comment thread, stored under an id unique in its thread.

created.description: When it was written, as a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, such as 2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z.

text.description: What it says, as text that isn't blank, without control characters but line breaks and tabs.

replies.description: The replies, by id, each with an author, a created time, and text.

comments.description: Comment threads, by id. Each one is pinned to a slide or a composition.

anchor-point.description: The point an object turns and scales about when it is animated or given an initial value, and the point a group tilts about.

x.description: How far across the frame, as a fraction of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame, as a fraction of its height.

auto-layout.description: How a group places its members one after another. Keys left out default to direction vertical, gap 0, align start, and reference point start. Members are placed in their order in the `objects` list. Hidden members, members with `ignore-auto-layout`, and lines attached to an object are skipped.

direction.description: Whether the members run down or across.

gap.description: The space between one member and the next.

align.description: How the members line up across the layout's direction.

reference-point.description: Which point of the members' box along the layout's direction stays at the position as they grow or shrink: its start, its middle, or its end.

position.description: The slide point, as {x, y}, where the members' box stands: its top-left corner in the group's turn, or its middle or end along the layout's direction by the reference point.

background.description: A slide background: a fill, an image, or an image on a fill.

fill.description: The color or gradient behind everything.

image.description: An image over the fill, as a presentation's file path. It covers the slide and is cropped as with an image's `scale-mode` `fill`.

crop.description: How far the image is zoomed, and which point stays in view.

prompt.description: The prompt for a generated background image.

image-style.description: The style of a generated background image, as text, or `none` for no style. The default is the presentation's `background-image-style`.

transparent-background.description: Whether a generated background image is made with a transparent background.

restyle.description: A style applied over the image. MarkdownPoint draws it from the image as it was first made.

generation.description: Which image generation record made the background image. For a restyle, it also names the image the restyle was applied to.

drop-shadow.description: A drop shadow behind the image.

exposure.description: How much lighter or darker the image is. 0 leaves it unchanged.

contrast.description: How much more or less contrast the image has. 0 leaves it unchanged.

saturation.description: How much more or less saturated the image's colors are. 0 leaves them unchanged.

temperature.description: How much warmer or cooler the image's colors are. 0 leaves them unchanged.

grayscale.description: How far the image's colors fade to gray. 0 leaves them unchanged.

color.description: a color role or a hex color

comment-author.description: Who wrote a comment. Its `id` takes one prefix per scheme: `local:` and a lowercase UUID for a computer's user, `shared:` and 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits for a collaboration service member, or `dropbox:` and a Dropbox account id as Dropbox's API spells it, which starts with `dbid:`.

id.description: Who wrote it, if known, in one of the record's three schemes.

name.description: The author's name, as the thread shows it, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

anyOf.description: A constraint that turns a model, or one of its nodes, toward a target, as Cinema 4D's Aim constraint does. Keys other than id, type, and target may be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as look, unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as constraints.look.strength.

node.description: The name of the model's node that turns, such as Head. Left out, the whole model turns.

target.description: The id of the model or light whose origin it turns toward, or `camera` to turn toward the camera.

axis.description: The axis of the model or node that points at the target, in its GLB's axes: y is up, and a model faces along +z. Left out, it's y.

strength.description: How far it turns toward the target, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. It acts on the result of the constraints before it. Left out, it's 1. A step can animate it.

anyOf.description: A constraint that keeps a model's volume as it scales, in the model's Local space. Volume is measured at the model's scale before animation. Keys other than id and type may be left out.

id.description: The constraint's id, such as squash, unique among the model's constraints. A step animates its strength as constraints.squash.strength.

mode.description: When the volume is kept. `strict` keeps it under any scale. `uniform` keeps it while the model scales evenly. `single-axis` keeps it while the free axis alone scales. Left out, it's strict.

free-axis.description: The axis whose scale is animated. The other two follow to keep the volume. Left out, it's y.

volume.description: The volume to keep, as a multiple of the model's volume before animation. Left out, it's 1.

strength.description: How strongly it keeps the volume, from 0, not at all, to 1, fully. Left out, it's 1. A step can animate it.

crop.description: An image's or a video's zoom and focus inside its frame.

scale.description: How far it is zoomed. At 1 the image sits in its frame as its scale-mode sets, and a background covers the slide. Above 1 it zooms in. Below 1 it zooms out.

focal-point.description: The point it keeps in view, {x, y}, each a fraction of the image across and down.

anyOf.description: A drop shadow, as Photoshop's Drop Shadow sets one: what the object paints grows solid by size × spread, then blurs by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. Its size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far it reaches, in canvas units, at most the widest the exported PDF draws as the canvas does: 102.878569 up to a shorter side of 1080, in proportion beyond, as 205.757138 at 3840 × 2160.

spread.description: The share of the size by which what casts the shadow grows solid before the rest of the size blurs, as Photoshop's Spread, where 1 stands solid all the way out.

offset.description: How far it falls, as {x, y} across and down in the object's own axes, turning and scaling with it and its groups but not mirrored by a flip. A background's is in the slide's axes.

color.description: Its color: a color role or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. The color carries no opacity, not even a role's: `opacity` alone sets how opaque the shadow is.

enter.description: Text that enters piece by piece, a piece a paragraph, a word, or a character, as `based-on` picks. Keys left out default to interpolation linear, order forward, spaces off, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 1.

delivery.description: `by-paragraph`: each paragraph enters on the step whose text cue names it. It takes based-on `paragraph`, no seed, and order, spread, pause, and progress only at their defaults.

duration.description: How long each paragraph takes to enter, in seconds. With interpolation hold, each paragraph shows as its cue is reached. A step that holds only paragraphs' cues lasts as long as they take.

from.description: How each piece looks as it starts to enter: opacity, x and y, scale, rotation, and blur.

x.description: How far across it starts, in ems.

y.description: How far down it starts, in ems.

scale.description: Its scale, where 1 is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned, in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is, its radius in ems. On the slide, it blurs no wider than the slide's widest blur, as `blur` says.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves into place: gradually on a curve, or at once with hold. A spring's response and an elastic's period don't apply here.

fade.description: The fade of each piece, as `{ length }`, a share of its travel. It follows the piece's interpolation.

length.description: How much of the piece's entrance the fade lasts, as a fraction. The fade starts with the move.

spaces.description: Whether each space counts as a piece and takes a turn. Only based-on `character` takes it.

order.description: The order the pieces enter in.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text holds between turns, once the pieces before have arrived.

progress.description: How far the text has entered. Steps animate it.

exit.description: Text that exits piece by piece, its pieces counted and timed as an entrance's. Keys left out default to interpolation linear, order forward, spaces off, spread 1, pause 0, and progress 0.

to.description: How each piece looks as it finishes exiting: opacity, x and y, scale, rotation, and blur.

x.description: How far across it ends, in ems.

y.description: How far down it ends, in ems.

scale.description: Its scale, where 1 is its own size.

rotation.description: How far it is turned, in degrees clockwise.

blur.description: How blurred it is, its radius in ems. On the slide, it blurs no wider than the slide's widest blur, as `blur` says.

interpolation.description: How each piece moves out of place: gradually on a curve, or at once with hold. A spring's response and an elastic's period don't apply here.

fade.description: The fade of each piece, as `{ length }`, a share of its travel. It follows the piece's interpolation.

length.description: How much of the piece's exit the fade lasts, as a fraction. The fade ends with the move.

spaces.description: Whether each space counts as a piece and takes a turn. Only based-on `character` takes it.

order.description: The order the pieces exit in.

seed.description: The seed for a random order: the same seed gives the same order.

spread.description: How many intervals each piece moves for. In forward, backward, or random order, this many move at once.

pause.description: How many intervals the text holds between turns, once the pieces before have left.

progress.description: How far the text has exited. Steps animate it.

flat-scale.description: A flat object's scale along its own axes, about its frame's center. Text breaks into lines first, then stretches with the scale.

floor-position.description: A floor's height in the 3D space: a floor lies level without end, as Cinema 4D's Floor does, so it takes y alone. Left out, the floor lies on the slide's bottom edge.

y.description: How far up from the slide's bottom edge, in canvas units.

frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only its x and y, and a text box's leaves out each side that grows to fit its text.

x.description: Where the left edge is, across. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

y.description: Where the top edge is, down. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

generation.description: How a generated or restyled image was made: the image shown is the one its image generation record made.

id.description: The id of the image generation record that made the image shown, the lowercase UUID its file `generated/<id>.json` is named by.

original.description: The image a restyle was applied to, there only when the record is a restyle's.

file.description: Its file path, as a presentation's file path, ending in an image's extension.

generation.description: How it was made, when it was generated. Left out, it wasn't.

id.description: The id of the image generation record that made it, the lowercase UUID its file `generated/<id>.json` is named by.

angle.description: A linear gradient's direction, in degrees clockwise from up.

line.description: Where a linear gradient's line lies, in the object's frame; the angle turns it about its middle. Left out, the line crosses the box the gradient fills through its center, as CSS's gradient line does.

x.description: Its middle's x, as a fraction of the frame's width.

y.description: Its middle's y, as a fraction of the frame's height.

length.description: Its length, as a fraction of the frame's diagonal.

stops.description: The gradient's colors, two or more, each with its position.

center.description: Where a radial gradient centers, as {x, y}.

x.description: Its x, as a fraction of the box's width: 0 is the left edge, 1 the right.

y.description: Its y, as a fraction of the box's height: 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom.

shape.description: `circle` keeps a radial gradient round in any box. Left out, the gradient reaches the box's corners.

stops.description: The gradient's colors, two or more, each with its position.

image-style-or-none.description: nonempty text without NUL characters, or "none"

line-end.description: A line end attached to an object.

object.description: The id of the object it attaches to.

side.description: Which side of the object it attaches to, or the nearest.

last-position.description: Where the end was when last drawn, as {x, y}. It's used when the object it attaches to isn't on the slide.

model-node-name.description: the name of one of the model’s nodes

nonblank-line.description: one line that isn’t blank and has no control characters

mask.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object’s frame

geometry.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object’s frame

text-path.description: SVG path data where 0 to 1 spans the object’s frame

file.description: a file path in the presentation’s folder

poster.description: a file path in the presentation’s folder

opaque-color.description: a color role or a hex color without opacity, such as "#000000"

repeater.description: Copies of the object, each moved, turned, scaled, and delayed a little more than the one before. Keys left out default to 0, except `scale` and `end-opacity`, which are 1, and `anchor-point`, the frame's center.

copies.description: How many there are, the original included.

position.description: How far each copy moves from the one before, as {x, y} across and down.

rotation.description: How far each copy turns from the one before, clockwise.

scale.description: How much each copy scales from the one before, where 1 keeps its size.

anchor-point.description: The point the copies turn and scale about, {x, y}, each a fraction of the frame across and down.

stagger.description: How much later each copy plays the object's animation than the one before.

end-opacity.description: The last copy's opacity, as a fraction of the object's own. The copies between fade toward it.

position-randomness.description: The farthest each copy moves in a random direction.

rotation-randomness.description: The farthest each copy turns either way at random.

scale-randomness.description: The most each copy grows or shrinks at random, as a fraction of its size.

stagger-randomness.description: The most extra time each copy waits at random.

seed.description: The random seed: the same seed gives the same copies.

restyle.description: A style applied over an image or a background's image, as a library style holds one.

name.description: The style's name, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

prompt.description: How the style changes an image, as an edit prompt that isn't blank.

transparent-background.description: Whether images in the style have transparent backgrounds.

space-euler.description: A 3D object's turn about its origin, in the 3D space's axes: x right, y up, and z toward the viewer, in degrees or, in quaternion mode, as a quaternion.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-position.description: A point in the 3D space, in canvas units: x runs right from the slide's left edge, y up from its bottom edge, and z toward the viewer, with the slide at z 0, right-handed as glTF and three.js define it. A parented object's position is in its parent's space.

space-quaternion.description: A 3D object's turn about its origin, in the 3D space's axes: x right, y up, and z toward the viewer, in degrees or, in quaternion mode, as a quaternion.

w.description: A quaternion's w, in quaternion mode only.

x.description: Degrees about x, or a quaternion's x.

y.description: Degrees about y, or a quaternion's y.

z.description: Degrees about z, or a quaternion's z.

space-scale.description: A 3D object's scale along its own axes, about its origin. A negative scale mirrors it along that axis. A light's scale also scales the objects parented to it, and an area light's surface.

items.description: One step: the moves, cuts, and media starts that a click or the previous step sets off. Its times, and its keyframes' and cues', are in seconds, rounded to six decimal places.

id.description: The step's id, unique on its slide.

name.description: The step's name in the Animate list, on one line that isn't blank and has no control characters.

start.description: When the step starts: with the previous step, or after it ends. On the first step, either starts it when the slide's transition ends, except under a scroll. Left out, it waits for a click.

min-duration.description: The least time the step lasts, in seconds. A later keyframe, cue, or entering paragraph extends it, and left out or 0, the step lasts as long as what it holds.

repeat-count.description: How many times the step plays before it completes. Left out, it plays once.

loop-from.description: Seconds into the step that it loops back to while waiting for the next click: before the later of its `min-duration` and its keyframe and cue times, not counting a paragraph's entrance.

additionalProperties.description: One property's animation in a step: its keyframes and what happens after the last one. A position can also be keyed as one point: `frame.xy` and `translation.xy` hold {x, y}, and `position.xyz` holds {x, y, z}, each keyframe holding every part. A step keys a position as a point or by its parts, not both: a step that keys both reads with a warning, and the point plays. An initial value sets each part on its own.

items.description: One keyframe: a value a property reaches at a time. Two keyframes of one property at one time read with a warning, and the later id plays. A keyframe's `null` clears its property, so its text style or default shows.

id.description: The keyframe's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

start.description: When the move into the keyframe begins, in seconds into the step. It must come before time. Left out, it begins at the previous keyframe.

time.description: When the property reaches the value, in seconds into the step.

value.description: The value, written as the property is. `null` clears a whole property, but never a part of one, a point, `visible`, `rotation`, `scale`, a constraint's strength, `shape-type`, `icon` or `geometry`.

interpolation.description: How the value reaches the keyframe: gradually on a curve, or at once with hold. It's a named curve, a named curve with its settings, a cubic Bézier, or a spring. Left out, linear.

interrupted.description: The longer move this keyframe interrupts. Up to this keyframe, the motion follows that move's curve.

end.description: When it would have ended, in seconds into the step, at or after the keyframe's time.

path.description: A curved motion path for the move into the keyframe. It goes on a point keyframe.

geometry.description: The path, as SVG path data from the move's start, 0 0, to its end, 1 0. It is one open contour of 2 to 8,192 points, in at most 1,048,576 characters.

orient.description: Whether the object turns to face along the path.

exponential-scale.description: Whether a scale move changes by a steady ratio, so a zoom looks even; from, to, or across 0, it moves at an even pace. Only `scale`, `scale.x`, `scale.y`, `scale.z`, and `crop.scale` take it.

oscillate.description: A wave added to the value from this keyframe to the next, or to the step's end. On a looping curve, the wave plays again each time around.

amplitude.description: How far the value swings either way, in the property's own unit.

frequency.description: How many full cycles each second.

phase.description: Where in its cycle the wave starts, 360 degrees to a cycle. Left out, it's 0.

wave-shape.description: The wave's shape. Left out, it's sine.

seed.description: The noise seed: the same seed gives the same noise. Left out, it's 0.

loop.description: How it loops after its last keyframe until the step ends: `repeat` replays from `loop-keyframe` to the last, and `ping-pong` plays that back and forth. Left out, it plays once.

loop-keyframe.description: The id of the keyframe the loop starts at, where its move begins if it has a `start`. Left out, or naming no keyframe of the curve, it is the first. It needs `loop`.

curves.description: The step's animation, by object and parameter, such as card.opacity.

items.description: An event at a set time in a step. A clip plays an Action of a model's or a 3D text's GLB `file`; a text built from an `extrusion` has none, so a clip on it plays nothing, with a warning.

id.description: The cue's id, unique in its step among its keyframes and cues.

time.description: When it happens, in seconds into the step.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model or a 3D text.

paragraph.description: The id of the paragraph that appears, as `<!-- id: … -->` ends its last line; a reader warns of an id no paragraph of the text carries.

object.description: The id of the object it acts on: for a clip, a model or a 3D text.

action.description: The name of the Action that a clip plays; an unnamed one is Animation 1, Animation 2, and on, in file order.

loop.description: `repeat` plays the Action again from its start each time it ends. Left out, it plays once.

clip-trim.description: The part of the Action that plays, as a start and an end in seconds into the Action.

stride.description: How far the model travels per cycle of its Action, in the GLB's meters. The Action's timing then follows the model's travel. A 3D text's clip ignores it.

blend-in.description: How long the clip takes to blend in fully over the model's current motion. Left out, it is fully blended in from its start.

clip-scale.description: How much longer a clip's Action plays than its file says, as Maya's Clip Scale: 2 is half speed, 0.5 double. Left out, it's 1. A model's clip with a stride ignores it.

cues.description: Events at set times in the step: a paragraph appearing, an audio object, a video, or a web video starting, or a clip playing an Action of a model or a 3D text.

color.description: The color: a color role or a hex color.

position.description: Where the color sits along the gradient, 0 to 1. Left out, the ends sit at 0 and 1, and the stops between spread evenly. A stop never stands before the one ahead of it.

table-frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only its x and y, and a text box's leaves out each side that grows to fit its text.

x.description: Where the left edge is, across. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

y.description: Where the top edge is, down. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

x.description: How far across the frame, as a fraction of its width.

y.description: How far down the frame, as a fraction of its height.

anyOf.description: A text's drop shadow, as Photoshop's Drop Shadow sets one, its lengths in ems of the text's font size. The letters grow solid by size × spread, then blur by a Gaussian whose standard deviation is size × (1 − spread) / √6. Its size isn't a blur radius.

size.description: How far past the letters the shadow reaches, as Photoshop's Size.

spread.description: The share of the size by which what casts the shadow grows solid before the rest of the size blurs, as Photoshop's Spread, where 1 stands solid all the way out.

offset.description: How far it falls from the letters, as {x, y} across and down in the text's own axes, turning and scaling with it and its groups.

color.description: Its color: a color role or a hex color written #RGB or #RRGGBB. The color carries no opacity, not even a role's: `opacity` alone sets how opaque the shadow is.

text-frame.description: An object's position and size, in canvas units from the slide's top left. A table's frame has only its x and y, and a text box's leaves out each side that grows to fit its text.

x.description: Where the left edge is, across. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

y.description: Where the top edge is, down. On a text box that grows to fit its text, it's the point the text grows from.

anyOf.description: A text's 3D model, in one of two forms: an `extrusion`, from which MarkdownPoint builds the words' letters into a model, or a GLB `file` a program built, with the `built-from` fingerprint of what it was built from. One unit of the model is one em of the text's size, and its origin stands on the first line's baseline at the left of the text's column. It moves, turns and scales with the text's frame, its depth by the square root of the text's two scales. A step's clips play the Actions of a GLB `file`, as they play a model's; an `extrusion` has none.

extrusion.description: The depth and bevel MarkdownPoint builds the words' letters to, in ems. An empty record builds them to its defaults.

depth.description: How far the letters stand out from the slide, in ems.

bevel.description: How far the letters' edges are rounded, in ems. 0 leaves them sharp.

anyOf.description: A text's 3D model, in one of two forms: an `extrusion`, from which MarkdownPoint builds the words' letters into a model, or a GLB `file` a program built, with the `built-from` fingerprint of what it was built from. One unit of the model is one em of the text's size, and its origin stands on the first line's baseline at the left of the text's column. It moves, turns and scales with the text's frame, its depth by the square root of the text's two scales. A step's clips play the Actions of a GLB `file`, as they play a model's; an `extrusion` has none.

file.description: The GLB a program built from the words, as a presentation's file path.

built-from.description: The fingerprint of what the GLB was built from, by the rule the reference gives. A rule this reader doesn't know reads as out of sync.

time-trim.description: The part of a video or audio file, or of a clip's Action, that plays.

start.description: Where it starts, in seconds into the file or the Action. Left out, it's 0.

end.description: Where it ends, in seconds into the file or the Action. It must come after start. Left out, it plays to the end.

transition.description: A slide transition. The defaults are interpolation ease-in-out, match object, direction left, color black, and delay 0.

start.description: When it starts. The default is a click. `automatically` starts it after the slide's last step.

delay.description: How long a transition that starts by itself waits after the slide's last step ends.

duration.description: How long it takes. It's left out when the effect is `none`.
